abstract: A 1-month-old infant died from extensive intracerebral hemorrhage due to a metastatic choriocarcinoma to the brain that presumably originated in the placenta. The clinical course was characterized by hyperbilirubinemia, repeated episodes of seizures, and intracranial hemorrhage. A computed tomographic scan revealed a large vascular mass in the left parieto-occipital region and a small lesion in the left frontal lobe. The placenta was expelled during the delivery and was not examined. In view of the high level of maternal human chorionic gonadotropic hormone and the autopsy finding of metastasis, we presumed that the mass was a metastatic choriocarcinoma that had originated in the maternal placenta. To our knowledge, only one previous instance of this phenomenon has been reported.
abstract_ja: 生後1か月の乳児が、胎盤由来と推定される転移性絨毛癌による脳の広範な出血で死亡した。臨床経過は高ビリルビン血症、反復するけいれん発作、頭蓋内出血を特徴とした。CT検査で左頭頂後頭部に大きな血管性腫瘤と、左前頭葉に小病変が認められた。胎盤は分娩時に排出され、検査されなかった。母体のヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)が高値であったことと、剖検で転移が確認されたことから、この腫瘤は母体胎盤に由来する転移性絨毛癌であると推定した。我々の知る限り、この現象の報告は以前に1例のみである。
